purpose: Evaluate later information by whether it improves the incumbent winner decision, not by whether it produces a cosmetically different probability.

core_identity.statement: Relative winner accuracy can change only on games where challenger and incumbent choose different winners.
core_identity.implication: A late horizon that rarely changes the pick can only create a small overall accuracy gain even with a strong switch win rate.

primary: paired winner accuracy delta versus T-120 F-ST
week-block uncertainty for paired zero-one loss
evaluation.same_pick_games: cannot affect relative winner accuracy; may still inform confidence-layer evaluation
evaluation.disagreement_games: decisive sample for whether later information should change the published winner pick

decision_policy.default: retain the T-120 F-ST winner pick
decision_policy.later_information_role: potential switch evidence, not automatic replacement
decision_policy.promotion_condition: A later horizon may become the winner-pick engine only after prospectively paired accuracy evidence supports a genuine positive accuracy delta versus T-120 F-ST. Better Brier alone is insufficient.
decision_policy.if_accuracy_unresolved: keep T-120 F-ST pick; later probability information may be used only in a separately validated confidence layer
decision_policy.conditional_switch_subgroups: not authorized in V1; any injury/QB/line-movement conditional switch rule requires a new preregistered candidate and fresh prospective start

historical_motivation.interpretation: The entire observed 3.0 winner-accuracy advantage over market came from a very small disagreement set, demonstrating why switch quality rather than global probability movement is the key accuracy-first object.
